report.tagline: A chat app for work where teams talk in channels instead of long email threads, now owned by Salesforce.
report.simpleSummary: Slack is like WhatsApp groups for your job, but organised. Each project or team gets a channel, everyone can search old messages, and you can plug in tools like Google Drive, Jira or GitHub. Small teams can start free, and companies pay per person per month for full history and AI features. It spread by teams starting it themselves, not by IT departments buying it.

overview.whatItDoes: Slack is a messaging app for work. Conversations happen in channels (by team, project or topic), direct messages and short audio or video huddles. Everything is searchable, and thousands of apps connect to it. Salesforce now sells it with AI that summarises channels and AI agents that do tasks inside Slack.
howItWorks: Someone creates a workspace for their team for free and invites coworkers by email.
People talk in channels like #marketing or #launch-q3 instead of email chains.
Apps and bots post updates from tools like Jira, GitHub, Google Drive and Salesforce.
Slack Connect lets two companies share a channel, such as a client and an agency.
The free plan shows only 90 days of history, which pushes growing teams to pay.
Paid plans add full history, AI summaries, admin controls and security.
overview.valueProposition: Less email, faster answers, and one searchable place where a team's work talk lives, with all the other tools plugged in.

businessModel.summary: Slack makes money from per-seat pricing: a monthly fee for each user. Teams start free, and they pay when they need full history, AI and admin features. Since 2025, Salesforce bundles Slack with its other products.

revenueStreams.detail: For small teams, about $7.25 to $8.75 per user per month.
About $15 per user per month on annual billing, with AI and more admin tools.
Custom-priced plans for large companies, with security and compliance.
Slack sold together with Salesforce CRM and Agentforce agents.

businessModel.pricing: Free plan with 90 days of history. Pro about $8.75 per user per month billed monthly. Business+ about $15 per user per month billed yearly. Enterprise+ and Enterprise Grid custom. Billing only for active users.
costDrivers: Cloud servers and storage for messages and files
AI model costs for summaries and agents
businessModel.unitEconomics: A 50-person team on Pro pays about 50 x $8.75 = $437 a month, or about $5,250 a year. Hosting their messages and files costs Slack a small fraction of that, maybe 10% to 20%, so gross margin is high. The big cost is getting the customer, but free sign-ups and teams inviting each other make that cheap for small teams. Large companies need sales teams and discounts, so their margin is lower. AI features add model costs per user. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Bottom-up adoption: one team starts free, then other teams join
Invites: every new member is invited by a coworker
Slack Connect: shared channels pull partner companies in
Salesforce selling Slack to its existing customers, and giving Salesforce users basic Slack access
whatBringsUsersBack: Bots and alerts from work tools
growth.moat: Once a company's conversations, integrations and workflows live in Slack, moving is painful. Slack Connect channels link companies to each other, adding network effects. But Microsoft Teams, bundled into Microsoft 365, weakens this moat in big companies.

pmLessons: Find the moment a user 'gets it', like 2,000 messages, and build the product to get every team there fast.
Bottom-up growth works when the product spreads by people inviting coworkers, not by selling to bosses.
Bundling can beat a better product: Teams caught up by coming free with Office.
Changing a free plan is risky; it can drive upgrades and also drive away your biggest fans.

interviewQuestions.question: Slack found that 2,000 messages predicts retention. How would you find a similar 'aha' metric for another product?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare retained vs churned users, find early actions that predict staying, check it is causal, then build onboarding around it.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Slack compete with Microsoft Teams in large companies?
interviewQuestions.hint: Don't fight on price alone. Focus on ecosystem, Slack Connect, AI agents, and the Salesforce bundle.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Slack make its free plan more generous?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh conversion revenue against top-of-funnel growth and brand. Suggest segment-specific plans and tests.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure if Slack AI is worth the price increase?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weekly AI use, time saved, renewal rates, net revenue retention.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to reduce notification overload.
interviewQuestions.hint: Identify personas, find what makes notifications useless, propose priority inbox or digests, guardrail on missed urgent messages.
